meta.title: The Abundance Funding World — Europe
meta.note: Curated from three research briefs (see /research). USD magnitudes are approximate and used for visual scaling; see each node for the sourced figure.

nodes.label: Good Ventures
nodes.blurb: The anchor private foundation of Facebook/Asana co-founder Dustin Moskovitz and Cari Tuna. ~$10B in assets, no full-time staff; grants on Coefficient's & GiveWell's recommendations. Single largest funder of effective altruism, farm-animal welfare and AI safety worldwide.

nodes.label: Patrick Collison / Stripe
nodes.blurb: Stripe co-founder/CEO. Named contributor to Coefficient's $120M Abundance & Growth Fund, co-founding donor of the Arc Institute, and launcher of the Progress Studies movement. The bridge between the EA/Open-Phil world and the abundance agenda.

nodes.label: Gates Foundation
nodes.blurb: Co-funder of the $125M Lead Exposure Action Fund. Bill Gates publicly endorsed the Open Philanthropy → Coefficient Giving rebrand in November 2025.

nodes.label: Lucy Southworth
nodes.blurb: Wife of Google co-founder Larry Page; a named new backer of the Lead Exposure Action Fund and the Strep A Vaccine Fund.

nodes.label: Navigation Fund
nodes.blurb: Newer public charity (Jed McCaleb, chaired by Seemay Chou) funding farm-animal welfare, AI safety and open science. Scaled from ~$4M (2023) to $60M+ (2025) and stepped into causes Good Ventures exited — the ecosystem's main diversification away from single-donor risk.

nodes.label: Jaan Tallinn / SFF
nodes.blurb: Skype co-founder; runs the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which shares many grantees with Coefficient. Early Anthropic investor and long-standing co-funder across the AI-safety field.

nodes.label: Coefficient Giving
nodes.people: CEO Alexander Berger · Chair Cari Tuna
nodes.blurb: Formerly Open Philanthropy — rebranded 18 Nov 2025. The research-and-grantmaking engine of the whole network. Directed over $1B in 2025 across ~13 multi-donor 'funds' other philanthropists can join. Keeps a London coworking hub and European-time-zone staff.

nodes.label: GiveWell
nodes.blurb: The charity evaluator co-founded in 2007 by Holden Karnofsky and Elie Hassenfeld; Good Ventures' other grant recommender and the lineage root of Open Philanthropy / Coefficient.

nodes.label: Abundance & Growth Fund
nodes.blurb: Launched March 2025. Good Ventures committed $60M, matched by Patrick Collison and two private funders. Absorbs Open Phil's housing (YIMBY) and innovation-policy work. Currently 'primarily in the United States' — international expansion is aspirational.

nodes.label: Lead Exposure Action Fund
nodes.blurb: $125M fund (LEAF) with the Gates Foundation and Lucy Southworth. LMIC-focused by design — no European grantees — e.g. a $17M grant to Pure Earth for lead exposure in India.

nodes.label: Navigating Transformative AI
nodes.blurb: Coefficient's AI programme — technical safety plus governance. Grantmaking scaled from ~$40M (2024) to over $140M (2025). The channel funding the UK/EU AI-policy beachheads and open to European applicants via its RFPs.

nodes.label: Farm Animal Welfare
nodes.blurb: Coefficient is 'the world's biggest funder of farm animal welfare', and Europe is its most active welfare region — the most concrete, euro-denominated way abundance-world money already lands in Europe.

nodes.label: Biosecurity & Pandemic Prep
nodes.blurb: Funds pandemic and biosecurity policy. The EU Biotech Act (Commission proposal Dec 2025) is the most plausible near-term European channel for Coefficient-funded influence, via grantees like CLTR.

nodes.label: Strep A Vaccine Fund
nodes.blurb: Newer multi-donor vaccine fund targeting $200M (~$140M raised at launch), anchored by Good Ventures, Lucinda Southworth, Adam & Abigail Winkel and the Patchwork Collective.

nodes.label: Arc Institute
nodes.blurb: Independent bio research institute (2021) co-founded by Patrick Collison, Silvana Konermann and Patrick Hsu; founding donors include Moskovitz & Tuna. Home of the Evo DNA foundation models and the Virtual Cell Initiative. The clearest node where the Collison and Good-Ventures money merge.

nodes.label: Institute for Progress
nodes.blurb: Washington DC metascience/innovation-policy think tank. Coefficient was a founding donor; it co-produced the 'Metascience 101' series with Berger, Clancy and Collison. The policy engine of the abundance agenda.

nodes.label: Emergent Ventures / Cowen
nodes.blurb: Tyler Cowen's fast-grant programme at the Mercatus Center — the intellectual hub of Progress Studies. Seeded Roots of Progress and Works in Progress and co-created Fast Grants with Collison.

nodes.label: Anthropic
nodes.blurb: The frontier AI lab at the centre of the network's interlock: Coefficient co-founder Holden Karnofsky is married to president Daniela Amodei and joined Anthropic in Jan 2025; Moskovitz and Tallinn were early investors. After a $65B Series H at a ~$965B valuation it filed confidentially for an IPO around June 2026 — the network's biggest potential future funding source, since an IPO would mint a wave of EA-aligned wealth.

nodes.label: BlueDot Impact
nodes.blurb: London AI-safety education org — the largest confirmed recent European AI-governance grant. Its mission: 'build the workforce needed to safely navigate transformative AI.'

nodes.label: Centre for Long-Term Resilience
nodes.blurb: UK AI & biosecurity policy institute. Coefficient pledged to match every £1 from other donors 1:1. CLTR submitted written evidence to the EU consultation informing the European Biotech Act (Nov 2025) — a direct US-money → EU-policy channel.

nodes.label: Talos Network
nodes.blurb: Brussels EU-AI-policy fellowship (the former EU Tech Policy Fellowship, which Open Phil helped launch). Historically the majority of its budget comes from Coefficient/Good Ventures. Places fellows at CEPS, The Future Society, OECD.AI and the EU AI Office.

nodes.label: The Future Society
nodes.blurb: Independent EU AI-governance think tank and a Talos placement host, active around the EU AI Act. Part of the Brussels cluster the network funds and staffs.

nodes.label: SaferAI
nodes.blurb: French AI-safety and risk-management organisation named in the EU AI-governance orbit (specific Coefficient grant unconfirmed post-database-deprecation).

nodes.label: Pour Demain
nodes.blurb: Swiss AI & biosecurity policy non-profit in the European GCR-policy network (specific Coefficient grant unconfirmed).

nodes.label: Eurogroup for Animals
nodes.blurb: The main EU farm-animal-welfare advocacy coalition in Brussels. €5.5M over three years plus fish-welfare (€1.63M), EU-trade-strategy (€1.23M) and chicken-welfare (€0.88M) grants — the single most-funded European animal node.

nodes.label: Compassion in World Farming
nodes.blurb: UK-founded, EU-wide farm-animal-welfare campaigner (~£2.73M over two years). One of the oldest cage-free advocacy organisations in Europe.

nodes.label: Animal Equality
nodes.blurb: International welfare NGO operating across Germany, Italy, Spain and the UK. Multiple Coefficient grants to expand EU work plus 'exit grants' for cage-free and broiler campaigns.

nodes.label: Equalia
nodes.blurb: Spanish farm-animal-welfare NGO that also runs the Animal Welfare Observatory. €2.37M over two years — the network's main Spanish beachhead.

nodes.label: Albert Schweitzer Foundation
nodes.blurb: German farm-animal-welfare foundation — $3M over two years of general support. The main German welfare beachhead.

nodes.label: L214
nodes.blurb: High-profile French animal-welfare NGO working on EU farm-animal-welfare legislation. Grant amount not public after the grants-database deprecation.

nodes.label: Progress Ireland
nodes.blurb: Think tank spearheaded by the Collisons in 2024 (CEO Sean Keyes) on housing, infrastructure and visa reform. John Collison's Oct-2025 Irish Times essay on planning/judicial-review sclerosis became a political event — the clearest sign the abundance agenda is being exported to Europe.

nodes.label: Works in Progress
nodes.blurb: London progress magazine acquired by Stripe (2022). Its editors — Sam Bowman, Ben Southwood, Saloni Dattani, Nick Whitaker — anchor the UK YIMBY/planning-reform node of the movement.

nodes.label: ARIA
nodes.blurb: The UK's DARPA-style Advanced Research and Invention Agency (Dominic Cummings' brainchild, operational 2023). Not Coefficient-funded, but shares the metascience DNA of Fast Grants/Arc — Cummings named Michael Nielsen as a potential leader. Included as an ecosystem-adjacent node.

nodes.label: Britain Remade
nodes.blurb: UK growth/YIMBY campaign. A Coefficient Abundance & Growth grant to a group like this would be the tell that the US-first abundance fund is internationalising into Europe — none exists yet. A leading indicator, drawn as a dashed 'watch' link.

nodes.label: EU AI Office
nodes.blurb: The European Commission body enforcing the EU AI Act. Talos fellows funded by the network are placed here and at OECD.AI — the point where abundance-world capital reaches inside EU institutions.

nodes.label: EU Biotech Act
nodes.blurb: European Commission legislative proposal (Dec 2025) following an Aug–Nov 2025 consultation with biosecurity provisions. CLTR — a Coefficient grantee — engaged the consultation, making this the network's most concrete biosecurity-policy channel into Europe.
